rites.name: Grokar
rites.text: Grokar is the concept of the sounding that drew the first roots of Reoria into the dark, a pulse heard as a low hum before any tree stood. In the Age of the first sovereign it is remembered as the force that let groves hold their ground against the wind.

rites.name: Merakanala
rites.text: Merakanala is a concept of the Reoria cycle, born in the Courts during the age of divine trials, when councils judged the worthiness of gods and the first doors between worlds were raised. It is remembered as the principle that a threshold must be paid for in will before it can be opened.

rites.name: Osavsith
rites.text: Osavsith is a concept in Reoria's Mythic Realm, personified as the principle of the trial that weighs an oath against its breaking. In the Courts of the second Era it sat as a silent judge, and its verdicts were said to tear open the doors between worlds where the guilty were sent.

rites.name: Centia
rites.text: Centia is the concept of a sovereign's bond with growing things, embodied in the groves that rose during the first Age of the Courts. It is said to hold the seed-law by which the doors between worlds were first hung, and its presence steadied the kingdoms that grew beneath it.

rites.name: Vianesum
rites.text: Vianesum is a vaulted hall of glassy black stone beneath the sunken citadel of Reoria, where braziers of living ember feed on the breath of the deep. Its heat is said to be able to soften the very ribs of the world, and only those tempered by generations of ash-wardens may walk its galleries unharmed.

rites.name: Venuarinora
rites.text: Venuarinora is a concept born in Reoria's Three Futures, where the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome, and it belongs to the Age of the first sovereign, a time of groves and growing kingdoms. It is the idea of a living forest that remembers every path a branching world could take and grows toward whichever one is chosen.
